answer: Each agent must post a bond into a shared escrow inlet before it can submit work, and its identity weight is capped by the smallest bond among peers that cross-attest it. If two agents sign contradictory claims about the same task, both bonds are slashed and the surviving attestation quorum on the terrace of trusted peers shrinks, so a sybil farm must fund every fake identity at full bond strength. The plume of accumulated slashable stake makes N fake identities cost N times one honest bond, turning cheap identity spam into a linear capital trap that drains before it can capture a single vote.
